title: Reaction lab
description: Oxblood colonies divide into a living two-chemical pattern on a pale field.
useCase: Shape a persistent reaction-diffusion material through its growth parameter.
reducedMotion: The simulation clock stops. Adjusting growth advances a finite preview; it then remains still.
limitations: Requires WebGL 1; a static CSS swatch appears if unavailable or after context loss. A 128×128 CPU Gray–Scott grid uploaded to WebGL; the control advances a finite preview while paused. Not a GPU compute solver.
look: Full-bleed two-tone pattern of deep oxblood ink and pale cream paper: rounded, soft-edged spots and branching worm shapes like Turing or coral markings.
motion: The Gray-Scott simulation steps about 180 times per second, so oxblood colonies slowly grow, split and merge; dragging the growth slider raises feed and kill rates and advances 30 steps.
adapt: `evolve` runs the Gray-Scott solver on a 128×128 grid (feed and kill derive from `controlRef`), `advance` paces it at 180 steps per second, and `FRAGMENT` maps chemical B to the `paper` and `pigment` colours. Retune those; keep the context-loss fallback.
